*All Out (2021)* was the third annual **All Out** professional wrestling pay-per-view (PPV) event produced by **All Elite Wrestling (AEW)**. It took place on **September 5, 2021**, at the **Now Arena** in Hoffman Estates, Illinois (a suburb of Chicago). The event was highly anticipated, featuring major matches, title defenses, and significant storylines leading into AEW's fall programming.

---

### **Key Details**
- **Date:** September 5, 2021
- **Venue:** Now Arena (Hoffman Estates, Illinois)
- **Attendance:** ~10,000 (sold out)
- **Buyrate:** One of AEW's highest-grossing PPVs at the time.
- **Main Event:** **Kenny Omega (c) vs. Christian Cage** for the **AEW World Championship**.
- **Other Major Matches:**
  - **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** (Punk’s first AEW singles match)
  - **Britt Baker (c) vs. Kris Statlander** for the **AEW Women’s World Championship**
  - **The Young Bucks (Matt & Nick Jackson) (c) vs. The Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix)** for the **AEW World Tag Team Championships** (Steel Cage Match)
  - **Miro (c) vs. Eddie Kingston** for the **AEW TNT Championship**
  - **Jon Moxley vs. Satoshi Kojima** (special attraction match)

---

### **Full Match Card & Results**
*(Winners in **bold**)*

1. **Pre-Show (Buy-In):**
   - **The Dark Order (Evil Uno & Stu Grayson) & Hangman Adam Page vs. The Factory (QT Marshall, Aaron Solow & Nick Comoroto)** – **Dark Order & Page won** (6-man tag)
   - **Paul Wight vs. QT Marshall** – **Wight won** (quick squash)
   - **Jurassic Express (Jungle Boy & Luchasaurus) vs. Private Party (Isiah Kassidy & Marq Quen)** – **Jurassic Express won** (tag team match)

2. **Main Card:**
   - **MJF vs. Brian Pillman Jr.** – **MJF won** (singles match)
   - **Britt Baker (c) (w/ Rebel & Jamie Hayter) vs. Kris Statlander** – **Baker retained** (AEW Women’s World Championship)
   - **Jon Moxley vs. Satoshi Kojima** – **Moxley won** (singles match)
   - **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** – **Punk won** (singles match)
   - **Miro (c) vs. Eddie Kingston** – **Miro retained** (AEW TNT Championship)
   - **The Young Bucks (c) vs. The Lucha Brothers (Penta & Fénix)** – **Lucha Brothers won** (Steel Cage Match for the AEW World Tag Team Championships)
   - **Kenny Omega (c) (w/ Don Callis) vs. Christian Cage** – **Omega retained** (AEW World Championship)

---

### **Major Storylines & Highlights**
1. **CM Punk’s AEW Debut Match**
   - Punk made his **long-awaited AEW debut** at *The First Dance* (August 20, 2021) and challenged Darby Allin to a match at All Out.
   - The match was **highly praised** for its storytelling, with Punk winning clean in his first singles match in **7 years** (since 2014 in WWE).
   - Punk’s return generated **massive buzz**, helping AEW break PPV records.

2. **The Lucha Brothers’ Cage Match Victory**
   - The **Lucha Brothers (Penta & Fénix)** defeated the **Young Bucks** in a **Steel Cage Match** to win the **AEW World Tag Team Championships**.
   - This was a **huge upset**, as the Bucks were the top babyface team in AEW.
   - The match was **brutal**, featuring **multiple high-risk spots** (including a **Canadian Destroyer** off the cage).

3. **Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage (AEW World Title)**
   - Christian Cage, a **legendary WWE star**, debuted in AEW earlier in 2021 and quickly rose up the ranks.
   - Omega retained after **interference from The Good Brothers (Karl Anderson & Doc Gallows)** and a **low blow**.
   - This match **elevated Christian** as a top contender and set up future feuds.

4. **Miro vs. Eddie Kingston (TNT Title)**
   - Miro, a **dominant champion**, defended against **Eddie Kingston** in a **hard-hitting match**.
   - Miro retained after **hitting a Game Over submission**, but Kingston’s performance was **praised for its intensity**.

5. **Britt Baker’s Women’s Title Defense**
   - Baker, AEW’s **top women’s star**, defended against **Kris Statlander** in a **physical match**.
   - Baker won after **assistance from Rebel & Jamie Hayter**, continuing her **heel run**.

6. **Jon Moxley vs. Satoshi Kojima**
   - A **dream match** between two **hard-hitting legends**.
   - Moxley won with a **Death Rider (paradigm shift)**, but the match was **short and impactful**.

7. **MJF’s Dominance**
   - MJF **destroyed Brian Pillman Jr.** in a **squash match**, continuing his **heel dominance**.
   - This set up his **future feud with Darby Allin** and eventual **push toward the AEW World Title**.

8. **Paul Wight’s Squash Match**
   - **Big Show (Paul Wight)** made his **AEW debut** and **dominated QT Marshall** in under **30 seconds**, showing his **power and comedic timing**.

---

### **Post-Event Fallout & Impact**
- **CM Punk’s Win** solidified him as a **top star** in AEW, leading to his **feud with MJF** and eventual **AEW World Title reign**.
- **The Lucha Brothers’ Tag Title Win** made them **one of AEW’s top teams**, leading to their **feud with Jurassic Express** and later **FTR**.
- **Christian Cage’s Strong Showing** kept him in the **World Title picture**, eventually leading to his **win over Kenny Omega** in 2022.
- **Miro’s TNT Title Reign** continued until he **lost to Sammy Guevara** in October 2021.
- **Britt Baker’s Women’s Title Run** lasted until **AEW Revolution 2022**, where she lost to **Thunder Rosa**.
- **The Young Bucks’ Loss** led to their **heel turn** and eventual **formation of the Elite** with Adam Cole.

---

### **Critical Reception & Ratings**
- **All Out 2021** was **widely praised** as one of AEW’s best PPVs at the time.
- **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** and **The Young Bucks vs. Lucha Brothers** were **standout matches**, receiving **4.5+ stars** from critics.
- The event **drew strong PPV buys**, helping AEW **compete with WWE’s SummerSlam** (which took place the same weekend).
- **Dave Meltzer’s Ratings:**
  - **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin – ★★★★½ (4.5 stars)**
  - **Young Bucks vs. Lucha Brothers – ★★★★¾ (4.75 stars)**
  - **Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage – ★★★★ (4 stars)**
  - **Miro vs. Eddie Kingston – ★★★★ (4 stars)**

---

### **Fun Facts & Trivia**
- This was **CM Punk’s first wrestling match in 7 years** (since 2014) and his **first AEW match ever**.
- **Paul Wight (Big Show)** signed with AEW in **February 2021** but made his **in-ring debut at All Out**.
- **Satoshi Kojima** was a **last-minute replacement** for Hiroshi Tanahashi, who had to pull out due to travel issues.
- The **Steel Cage Match** was the **first in AEW history** and set a **new standard for tag team wrestling**.
- **MJF’s post-match promo** (where he **mocked CM Punk**) was a **huge moment**, leading to their **future feud**.

---

### **Legacy of All Out 2021**
- **CM Punk’s return** was a **game-changer** for AEW, bringing in **new fans** and **mainstream attention**.
- The **Lucha Brothers’ title win** helped **elevate AEW’s tag division**.
- The event **proved AEW could deliver big-money PPVs** and **compete with WWE** in terms of star power.
- Many of the **storylines from All Out 2021** (Punk vs. MJF, Lucha Brothers’ reign, Christian’s rise) **carried into 2022 and beyond**.
